To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the magneto-optical response of HgSe is dominated by the plasma frequency, (ii) the plasma frequency in HgSe is strongly modified by the magnetic field, (iii) the plasma edge is shifted by the magnetic field and its dispersion-like behaviour is caused by the magnetic-field-induced anisotropy, and (iv) the phonon-related structure is shifted by the field in an unusual manner.

We investigate the lowenergy magneto-optical response of HgSe doped with Cr by means of farinfrared reflectivity in magnetic fields up 20 T.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the low-energy magnetics-optical properties of semiconductors with a high density of free charge carriers.
the low-energy magnon excitations in HgSe and the magneto-plasma edge, helicon waves, and the phonon-related structure observed in the reflectivity spectra.
a theoretical description of the low-energy magneticspectra of HgSe in the presence of a magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the low-energy magneticspectra of HgSe can be explained within the framework of a simple model, where the magnetic field dependence of the dielectric function is determined only by the field-induced change of the electron and hole densities.
the observed effects in HgSe can be attributed to the presence of the Cr ions, which introduce a magnetic field-dependent dieletric function.
a dynamic dielectric function is a very powerful tool to investigate the magneto-optics of semiconductors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed magneto-optical phenomena in HgSe can be explained by a simple model, which is based on a dynamic dielectric function.
we have found a new mechanism of the magnetic field-induced changes in the dielectric function of semiconductors, which can be described by the dynamic theory of the magnetoplasmon.
we could show that the magnetic field dependence of the phonon frequency is a direct result of the magnetic field dependence on the carrier density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic field dependence of the dielectric function can be described by the same model as that used to describe the dielectric function at zero magnetic field.
the magnetic field-induced effects are much larger than the effects of the Cr impurities.
the phonon-related structure can be explained by the presence of a magnetic field-induced gap in the electronic spectrum of HgSe.
